items.title: Lee Collins Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: And my, what a good feeling in my life, with my wife right there, little Mary, little Mary.

ctx.x: But, there was no happy days in the world of playing like the good old New Orleans days. When they had that good old real ragtime funky jazz music day. But the funny thing Bill, New Orleans ain't got it no more. They ain't got the jazz. I don't know. Young kids, young boys don't look like they go, they don't want to fall in those timers shoes. They don't play that kind of music. They have a different style. But the other boys, like my boy Tony Peretti, another good boy, they all trying to carry the traditional…

items.title: Mary Collins Interview, 1974-09-29
items.q: He told me to take down everything he would tell me. Sometimes he would write it on himself, longhand. And I would type it up.

ctx.x: A classic by Little Brother Montgomery, to say the least. And I'd like to remind you, this is WLDC at Loyola University, and we're in New Orleans. And we're doing an interview with Mrs. Lee Collins, whose husband is Trumpeter Lee Collins. And she has written a book, and it's entitled, Oh, Didn't He Ramble? And we're trying to talk about Lee and something about the book and get into a few things about it. What inspired you to write a book about your husband? Well, Lee.
He did it himself. Lee wanted it written. He wanted it written. He told me to take down everything he would tell me. Sometimes he would write it on himself, longhand. And I would type it up.
